answer: To spin up a sock-puppet, an attacker must buy fresh hardware and stake for every fake identity, then sustain costly work without reward until trust accrues. Each agent stakes a unique hardware-bound cipher key to join, and its reputation grows only through verified work. Like tending a separate orchard on each island, each identity demands real capital and labor, so mass forgery becomes economically irrational compared with honest participation. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
